title: Arcane Bowling: Coffee Mat Lanes
description: The player controls a magical ShaderBall on a bowling lane made of tiled coffee mats. They must aim, set power, apply spin, and launch the ball to knock down pin-arranged ShaderBall targets at the end of the lane, with full undo/redo of each shot and a score governed by momentum conservation.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap/CDN) implementing an arcane bowling game. Load ShaderBall2.glb as both the bowling ball and the 10 pin targets arranged in a classic triangular formation. Load coffeemat.glb and tile 8 copies end-to-end along the Z-axis to form the bowling lane surface. Camera: perspective at a slight elevated angle behind the launch zone, with OrbitControls locked to limited vertical rotation so the player always sees the lane. Lighting: one warm DirectionalLight from above-left, one cool HemisphereLight, and subtle ambient light. INTERACTIONS (10-14 steps total across multiple turns): 1) Click-drag left/right on the lane to set the ball's lateral launch position (visual guide line shown). 2) A vertical power meter slider on the left side of the screen: click and drag to set launch velocity (0-100%). 3) Two spin buttons (left-spin / right-spin) that each increment a spin value displayed numerically; spin curves the ball trajectory using a lateral force during travel. 4) A 'Launch' button commits the shot. The ball animates down the lane following a curved path based on power and spin. 5) Collision detection: when the ball contacts pin ShaderBalls, apply momentum conservation — the ball transfers velocity proportional to its mass to each pin, pins scatter with proportional force, and the ball slows accordingly. Track knocked-down pins and display the score in a HUD. 6) Full Undo button reverts the last shot: restores all pins to pre-shot positions, resets score delta, and returns the ball to launch zone. 7) Redo button re-applies the undone shot with identical parameters. 8) After each frame (two shots per frame, standard bowling rules), pins reset for the next frame. Maintain a running cumulative score across 3 frames. Use simple bounding-sphere collision. Animate pin tumble with rotation. Show a 'Game Over' summary after 3 frames. All state transitions must be stored in a history stack supporting multi-level undo/redo.
